Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: a brand kit — let a customer supply their own logo and colours so generated sites look like *their* business rather than a nice generic template.

## The constraint that decides the whole design
Generated sites are static files under a CSP with **no external hosts**: `default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'` and **no `font-src`**. Read `app/api/site/[slug]/[[...path]]/route.ts` yourself. Consequences you must work within:
- A logo must be **inlined** — SVG markup or a data URI. There is no remote image and no upload CDN.
- **Custom web fonts are impossible, including base64 ones**: with no `font-src`, fonts fall back to `default-src 'self'`, which does not admit `data:` the way `img-src` does. Do not build a font picker.
- Everything the builder writes passes through the model's context as tokens, so **size is cost**. A 200 KB base64 PNG logo is roughly 270 KB of base64 in a prompt. Work out what is actually affordable and say so with numbers.

## Read before designing
- `lib/assets/patterns.ts` — 30 curated gradients and palettes with stable ids already exist. **Reuse them as the palette vocabulary**; do not invent a second one.
- `lib/agent.ts` SYSTEM — how the builder is instructed, including its rules against inventing business facts. **READ ONLY.**
- `lib/foundation.ts` — the starting project, including `src/index.css`. Tailwind v4 uses an `@theme` block; a palette can be seeded there as CSS variables, which is far cheaper than describing colours in prose. **READ ONLY.**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `ProjectFile.content` is a `String`, so an SVG logo can live there as an ordinary project file. **You may not change the schema**; work within it.
- `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx` — there is already an image-attach path that downscales client-side to a data URL. Learn from it; do not duplicate it.

## Build
1. **`lib/brand-kit.ts`** — the model: a logo (SVG preferred, raster accepted with a hard size cap you justify), a palette chosen from the existing catalogue or as explicit hexes, and a business name. Plus the code that turns a brand kit into (a) a `@theme` block for `src/index.css` and (b) a short, precise instruction fragment for the prompt.
2. **An API route** under `app/api/projects/[id]/brand/` to read and write a project's brand kit. Auth via `requireUser()`, ownership scoped in the same query as the id — match the convention in `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts`.
3. **A UI** under `components/brand/` to set it.

## Hard requirements
- **An uploaded SVG is untrusted input and SVG is executable.** It can carry `<script>`, `onload=`, `<foreignObject>`, external `href`s and entity expansion. It will be inlined into a page served on `*.kodely.site`. **Sanitise it server-side** — allowlist elements and attributes, do not blocklist — and say exactly what you allow. Getting this wrong is stored XSS on a customer's own site. There is no sanitiser dependency available; hand-roll it and be conservative. If you are not confident, restrict to a very small element set and say so.
- **Colour must reach the model as exact hex values plus a catalogue preset id, never as adjectives.** "Warm and modern" produces exactly the generic look this feature exists to kill.
- **State the token cost** of whatever logo format you allow, with real arithmetic.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT: `lib/brand-kit.ts`, `app/api/projects/[id]/brand/**`, `components/brand/**`
DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, any other lib file, other app/api routes, app/projects/** (another agent is in there — if the editor needs an entry point, describe the exact line), app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.

## Constraints
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast — known accepted issue). Real labels, visible `focus-visible:` states, no keyboard traps.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must stay clean — currently ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.** Other agents are active in `lib/credits.ts`, `app/api/generate/route.ts`, `app/projects/[id]/**`, `app/api/site/**`; transient errors there are not yours.
- Verify with a real project you create and delete. **Test your SVG sanitiser against actual attack payloads** — script tags, event handlers, `javascript:` hrefs, `<foreignObject>`, nested entities — and report what each one did.

## Report back
Your sanitiser allowlist and the payloads you tested with results, the logo size cap and its token arithmetic, how colour reaches the model, what you need outside your scope, and anything you refused to build.

343	  /** Fill of the divider shape — normally the colour of the *next* section. */

352	/**
353	 * A full-bleed `<svg>` divider. Drop it at the very bottom of a section with
354	 * the *following* section's background colour as `fill`.
355	 */
356	export function dividerSvg(id: string, opts: DividerRenderOptions = {}): string | null {
357	  const preset = DIVIDERS.find((d) => d.id === id);
358	  if (!preset) return null;
359	  const { fill = "currentColor", height = 90, flipX = false, flipY = false, className } = opts;
360	  const sx = flipX ? -1 : 1;
361	  const sy = flipY ? -1 : 1;
362	  const tx = flipX ? 1440 : 0;
363	  const ty = flipY ? 120 : 0;
364	  const transform = flipX || flipY ? ` transform="translate(${tx} ${ty}) scale(${sx} ${sy})"` : "";
365	  // `block w-full` rather than an inline style: a style attribute is a string
366	  // in HTML but must be an object in JSX, so it would break the moment the
367	  // markup is pasted into a .tsx file. `display:block` matters here — an
368	  // inline svg otherwise sits on the text baseline and leaves a gap under the
369	  // divider.
370	  const cls = `${className ? className + " " : ""}block w-full`;
371	  return (
372	    `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="${DIVIDER_VIEWBOX}" preserveAspectRatio="none"` +
373	    ` width="100%" height="${height}" aria-hidden="true" class="${cls}">` +
374	    `<path d="${preset.d}" fill="${fill}"${transform}/></svg>`
375	  );
376	}

501	  build: (color = DEFAULT_PATTERN_COLOR, s = size) => build(color, s),
502	}));

504	export function getPattern(id: string): PatternPreset | undefined {
505	  return PATTERNS.find((p) => p.id === id);
506	}

508	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
509	// Initials avatars. Deterministic from a name, so the same person gets the
510	// same colour on every page and across rebuilds.
511	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
512	
513	/** FNV-1a. Small, stable, and good enough to spread names across a hue wheel. */
514	function hash(input: string): number {
515	  let h = 0x811c9dc5;
516	  for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i++) {
517	    h ^= input.charCodeAt(i);
518	    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193) >>> 0;
519	  }
520	  return h;
521	}
522	
523	/** Up to two initials: "Ada Lovelace" -> "AL", "cheryl" -> "C". */
524	export function initialsOf(name: string): string {
525	  const words = name.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
526	  if (words.length === 0) return "?";
527	  if (words.length === 1) return words[0].slice(0, 2).toUpperCase();
528	  return (words[0][0] + words[words.length - 1][0]).toUpperCase();
529	}
530	
531	export type AvatarColors = { from: string; to: string; text: string };
532	
533	/**
534	 * A deterministic two-stop colour pair for a name. Saturation and lightness
535	 * are fixed so every avatar in a list has the same weight — only the hue moves.
536	 */
537	export function avatarColors(name: string): AvatarColors {
538	  const h = hash(name.toLowerCase());
539	  const hue = h % 360;
540	  // Skip the 55-90deg band, where mid-lightness yellows go muddy against white text.
541	  const safeHue = hue > 55 && hue < 90 ? hue + 40 : hue;
542	  return {
543	    from: `hsl(${safeHue} 62% 52%)`,
544	    to: `hsl(${(safeHue + 28) % 360} 58% 40%)`,
545	    text: "#ffffff",
546	  };
547	}
548	
549	export type AvatarOptions = {
550	  size?: number;
551	  /** "circle" (default) or "rounded". */
552	  shape?: "circle" | "rounded";
553	  className?: string;
554	};
555	
556	/** An inline `<svg>` initials avatar — no image, no request, no layout shift. */
557	export function initialsAvatarSvg(name: string, opts: AvatarOptions = {}): string {
558	  const { size = 64, shape = "circle", className } = opts;
559	  const { from, to, text } = avatarColors(name);
560	  const initials = initialsOf(name);
561	  // The gradient id must be unique per name so two avatars on one page don't
562	  // collide — SVG gradient ids are document-global.
563	  const gid = `av${hash(name).toString(36)}`;
564	  const bg =
565	    shape === "circle"
566	      ? `<circle cx="32" cy="32" r="32" fill="url(#${gid})"/>`
567	      : `<rect width="64" height="64" rx="16" fill="url(#${gid})"/>`;
568	  const cls = className ? ` class="${className}"` : "";
569	  return (
570	    `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64" width="${size}" height="${size}"` +
571	    ` role="img" aria-label="${name.replace(/[<>&"]/g, "")}"${cls}>` +
572	    `<defs><linearGradient id="${gid}" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="1">` +
573	    `<stop offset="0%" stop-color="${from}"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="${to}"/></linearGradient></defs>` +
574	    bg +
575	    `<text x="32" y="33" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="central" fill="${text}"` +
576	    ` font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif" font-size="${
577	      initials.length > 1 ? 26 : 30
578	    }" font-weight="600" letter-spacing="0.5">${initials}</text></svg>`
579	  );
580	}
581	
582	/**
583	 * The CSS-only form: a gradient background plus the initials as text. Cheaper
584	 * than the SVG when the avatar is already a React element.
585	 */
586	export function initialsAvatarCss(name: string): { css: string; initials: string } {
587	  const { from, to, text } = avatarColors(name);
588	  return {
589	    initials: initialsOf(name),
590	    css: `background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, ${from}, ${to}); color: ${text};`,
591	  };
592	}

2	// Principles baked in here (see the Kodely board):
3	//  - every generation is a Build row with real token counts, so cost per build is never a guess
4	//  - credits are a ledger, never a mutable counter: the balance is derivable and auditable
5	//  - failed builds are recorded but NEVER charged

8	  provider = "prisma-client-js"
9	}

13	  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")

18	  email            String   @unique
19	  // Nullable because a Google-only account never sets a local password.
20	  passwordHash     String?
21	  googleId         String?  @unique

26

28	  // This is the user's own guard against a runaway session, not a plan limit —
29	  // bill shock is the category's deepest trust wound (one competitor billed
30	  // $607 against a $25 plan in three days), and a cap the user sets themselves
31	  // is the cheapest honest answer to it.

34	  // Set when the user asks for erasure, cleared if they cancel. The grace
35	  // period is measured from here.

37	  // Exists because the alternative was worse: the request was being recorded as
38	  // marker-prefixed SupportNote rows, which then appeared in an operator-notes
39	  // UI that describes itself as "operator-written, never customer-facing" — one

51	// First-party analytics. Self-hosted deliberately: cheaper, keeps the data
52	// ours, avoids another paid API on the critical path, and is privacy-clean.
53	//
54	// One wide table rather than a table per dashboard, because the activation
55	// funnel, retention cohorts, per-user journey, attribution and the overview
56	// tiles are all different queries over the same stream. Build it once, or
57	// every dashboard invents its own tracking.

59	  id     String  @id @default(cuid())
60	  // Nullable so pre-signup events (landing view, prompt submitted) still land.
61	  userId String?

63	  name   String

70	
71	  // Funnels scan by name over a window; journeys scan one user over a window.
72	  @@index([name, createdAt])
73	  @@index([userId, createdAt])
74	}

76	// A submission from a form on a PUBLISHED generated site.
77	//
78	// This is the one deliberate hole in "generated sites have no backend", and it
79	// exists because the alternative is worse: the builder is currently forbidden
80	// from drawing a contact form at all, because a form that silently discards a
81	// real enquiry is worse than no form — and a live blog post already told dental
82	// practices their appointment requests were arriving when they were not.
83	//
84	// Submissions land HERE, on Kodely's origin, never on the customer's site. The
85	// generated page stays static; only the POST target is ours.
86	model FormSubmission {
87	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
88	  projectId String
89	  /// Which form on the page, when a site has more than one.
90	  formName  String   @default("contact")

98	  readAt DateTime?

100	  /// positive is recoverable and the rate is measurable.
101	  spam   Boolean @default(false)
102	
103	  project Project @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

109	// Pre-auth attempt counter for login and signup.

115	// resets on every deploy and multiplies by the process count.
